title: Low‑Carb Holiday Feast: Spiralized Brussels Sprouts Side Dish
meta_description: Discover a festive low‑carb side that dazzles the table: spiralized Brussels sprouts with garlic, lemon, and toasted almonds—perfect for holiday meals.
html:
When the holidays call for a side dish that’s both festive and low‑carb, spiralized Brussels sprouts take center stage. This crisp, garlicky, and lightly lemon‑brightened side not only adds color to your plate but also makes the most of the vegetable’s natural flavor. Using a vegetable spiralizer—handheld or countertop—turns these mini‑cabbages into elegant ribbons that cook in minutes, keeping the holiday feast light without sacrificing taste.

Why Choose Spiralized Brussels Sprouts for a Holiday Side?

Brussels sprouts are already a holiday staple, but spiralizing them changes the texture and presentation entirely. The thin ribbons absorb sauces faster than whole sprouts, allowing each bite to be perfectly seasoned. Because the vegetable stays low in carbs and high in fiber, it pairs well with richer holiday proteins without adding unwanted calories. Plus, the visual appeal of a spiraled nest of greens instantly elevates any spread.

Essential Tools: The Vegetable Spiralizer

The only tool you truly need for this recipe is a reliable vegetable spiralizer. Whether you opt for a compact handheld model for quick prep or a larger countertop version for batch cooking, the spiralizer will give you uniform strands that cook evenly. It’s also handy for future low‑carb meals—think zucchini noodles, carrot ribbons, or cucumber spirals. Having a dedicated spiralizer means you’ll spend less time fiddling with a knife and more time enjoying the holiday vibe.

Ingredients

  • 1 pound Brussels sprouts, trimmed
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • Zest and juice of 1 lemon
  • 1/4 cup sliced almonds, toasted
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • Optional: 1/2 teaspoon red‑pepper flakes for a subtle kick

Step‑by‑Step Preparation

1. Prep the sprouts. Rinse the Brussels sprouts, trim the stem ends, and cut off any outer leaves that look wilted. Halve the sprouts lengthwise; this makes them easier to feed through the spiralizer.

2. Spiralize. Assemble your vegetable spiralizer according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Feed the halved sprouts through the blade that creates thin ribbons (often labeled “medium” or “julienne”). If you’re using a handheld model, simply twist the sprout against the blade. Collect the spiraled strands in a bowl.

3. Toast the almonds. While the sprouts are spiraling, place the sliced almonds in a dry skillet over medium heat. Stir constantly for 2‑3 minutes until golden and fragrant. Transfer to a plate and set aside.

4. Sauté the garlic. In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté for about 30 seconds—just until aromatic, not browned.

5. Cook the spiraled sprouts. Add the Brussels sprout ribbons to the skillet, tossing to coat them in the garlic‑oil mixture. Cook for 3‑4 minutes, stirring frequently, until the strands are just tender but still retain a slight crunch.

6. Finish with lemon and seasoning. Remove the skillet from heat. Stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, and red‑pepper flakes if using. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

7. Plate and garnish. Transfer the warm spiraled Brussels sprouts to a serving dish. Sprinkle the toasted almonds over the top for added texture and a nutty finish.

Tips for Perfect Holiday Success

• Don’t over‑cook. The key to a satisfying side is maintaining a slight bite. Overcooking turns the ribbons mushy and dulls their natural sweetness.

• Season in layers. Adding a pinch of salt after each cooking step helps the flavors penetrate the vegetable strands more evenly.

• Make ahead. You can spiralize the sprouts and toast the almonds a day before the feast. Store the spiraled sprouts in an airtight container with a drizzle of olive oil to prevent drying. Re‑heat gently in a skillet just before serving.

• Swap ingredients. If you don’t have almonds, try crushed walnuts or pepitas. For a richer flavor, finish with a drizzle of melted butter instead of olive oil.

Pairing Suggestions

This spiralized Brussels sprouts holiday side shines alongside roasted turkey, honey‑glazed ham, or a succulent prime rib. Its bright lemon notes cut through richer sauces, while the toasted almonds echo the crunch of a holiday stuffing. For a fully low‑carb menu, serve it with cauliflower mash and a green bean almondine—still festive, still light.

FAQ

Can I use a regular kitchen slicer instead of a vegetable spiralizer?

Yes, a mandoline with a julienne blade will produce similar ribbons, but a dedicated vegetable spiralizer guarantees uniform thickness and faster prep, especially when handling larger batches for holiday gatherings.

Is it okay to freeze the spiraled Brussels sprouts?

Freezing is possible, but the texture changes after thawing, becoming softer. If you need to store them, keep them raw in a sealed bag without any seasoning, and use within a month for the best bite.

What if I don’t have fresh lemon?

A splash of high‑quality bottled lemon juice works, but fresh zest adds an aromatic punch that bottled juice alone can’t match. If you’re out of both, a drizzle of white wine vinegar can provide a similar acidity.
